name: Mu Digital AZND
oneLiner: AZND is Mu Digital's KYC-gated dollar token; users lock it in the loAZND vault for Asia credit yield, with muBOND absorbing first losses.
collateral: The last Accountable snapshot Pharos ingested showed the Asset Pool concentrated in short-term cash and liquid bonds; Mu Digital's published mandate still targets an Asia credit portfolio with illiquid private credit capped at 20%, and the muBOND junior tranche overcollateralizes AZND at ~118%
pegMechanism: KYC-gated 1:1 mint using USDC, USDT, or AUSD; redemptions processed weekly (~7 calendar days) per Singapore fund liquidity calendar; muBOND junior tranche absorbs NAV losses first; insurance fund provides additional backstop; permissionless secondary swaps via DEX partners on Monad

reserveReview.rationale: Re-verified the Mu Digital litepaper pages on 2026-07-20: the yield-mechanics page commits the Asset Pool to Asia-Pacific government (min BBB), corporate IG (min BBB-), bank (senior and subordinated), and high-yield (min BB) bonds plus private credit, and the risk framework caps illiquid private credit at 20% with a blended BBB target and average duration ~5. The 80.9% short-term cash / 19.1% liquid bonds split from the last checked-in Accountable snapshot remains the most recent constituent-level envelope; no newer dated snapshot was fetchable today. The 'Liquid Bonds' slice keeps the high tier: the documented mandate spans subordinated bank debt and BB high yield, the snapshot does not break out ratings, and under the uncertain-choose-riskier rule the credit taxonomy tier is retained rather than assuming an IG-only book. Redemptions run on a weekly Singapore fund calendar (~7 calendar days), so bond liquidity is mapped to seven-days.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Latest checked-in Accountable snapshot (80.9/19.1 envelope) re-checked against Mu Digital litepaper disclosures fetched 2026-07-20
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The static envelope is disclosed, but the snapshot date, fund-level constituent identities and ratings mix, custody allocation, valuation reconciliation, and loss-recovery execution terms are not fully published in the reviewed materials.

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-3 (lead usdd-tron-dao-reserve)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: Mu Digital's litepaper (fetched 2026-07-20) states the Asset Pool is managed by GHAM under a MAS Capital Markets Services licence and held in a regulated fund vehicle, but it does not name the fund's custodian bank, sub-custodians, or the prime broker that provides the documented liquidity credit lines. The transparency page commits to Pennyworks NAV accounting and to onchain Treasury Wallets 'segregated from the Company's operational funds', but it documents no trust, SPV, or holder-claim structure for the fund assets themselves, so segregation and bankruptcy-remoteness terms are unpublished. No rehypothecation or collateral-reuse terms are disclosed for either the bond portfolio or the prime-broker credit lines. Provider shares are not published; the 80.9/19.1 reserve envelope carries no custody split.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: AZND moves between Ethereum and Monad as a native LayerZero V2 Omnichain Fungible Token (burn-on-source / mint-on-destination), confirmed by the verified Ethereum implementation (0x2E49c14A) inheriting @layerzerolabs/oft-evm-upgradeable OFTUpgradeable whose _debit burns and _credit mints, wired to the canonical LZ V2 EndpointV2, and by a live ETH<->Monad message flow on LayerZeroScan (15+ delivered, ~24 messages/24h). It is a pure OFT, not an OFT Adapter/lockbox. The OApp runs a custom (non-default) DVN security stack on the Monad pathway (EID 30390) using named LayerZero DVNs (Deutsche Telekom, LayerZero Labs, Canary, plus Frax/Horizen), placing it in the external-validated-network tier. (Exact required/optional DVN counts and threshold were not independently byte-confirmed from getConfig.)

Canonical AZND on Monad (verified 2026-07-20, block 88903152): token 0x4917a5ec9fcb5e10f47cbb197abe6ab63be81fe8 (symbol AZND) with no LayerZero endpoint surface; minting runs through the PrimaryMarket minter contract 0xe64730de04aeaf8d3892 per the verified mint-authority review, administered by the MU Digital AccessManager default admin 0x8b5f269f68d42490dee19fc4ab275cdd80940068.

mintAuthority.summary: AZND primary issuance is KYC-gated by Mu Digital, while the Monad token's mint function is available to three current TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE holders: the PrimaryMarket contract, one EOA, and one EIP-7702 delegated EOA. The Monad AccessManager default admin can change that role set. Ethereum AZND is a UUPS LayerZero OFT spoke whose owner can change trusted peers and whose AccessManager default admin can upgrade mint-critical logic; both controls currently resolve to the same Mu Digital EOA.

controls.label: Monad AZND PrimaryMarket minter
controls.evidence: At Monad block 87687688, AZND 0x4917a5ec...1fE8 returned immutable PRIMARY_MARKET 0xe64730de...0c89 and AccessManager 0x7b14860e...b47f; the AccessManager returned true for TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE on the PrimaryMarket. Verified AZND source restricts mint(receiver, amount) to TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE, while Mu Digital documents PrimaryMarket as its KYC-gated mint/redeem contract.

controls.label: Monad AZND TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE EOA
controls.evidence: At Monad block 87687688, AccessManager 0x7b14860e...b47f returned true for TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE on 0xf6e5255f...1ca8. The account had no deployed bytecode at that block. Verified AZND source allows every current TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE holder to call mint(receiver, amount) without an onchain amount cap.

controls.label: Monad AZND TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE delegated EOA
controls.evidence: At Monad block 87687688, AccessManager 0x7b14860e...b47f returned true for TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE on 0x8b33f017...bd0b. Its 23-byte 0xef0100 delegation designator points to 0x63c0c19a...ae32b, identifying an EIP-7702 delegated EOA rather than a standalone contract authority. Verified AZND source permits this role holder to call uncapped mint(receiver, amount).

controls.label: Monad AccessManager default admin
controls.evidence: At Monad block 87687688, AccessManager 0x7b14860e...b47f returned true for DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on 0x8b5f269f...0068, which had no deployed bytecode. Verified AccessManager source makes DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE the admin for role grants and revocations, so this EOA can change AZND's TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE holder set.

controls.label: Ethereum AZND OFT owner and UUPS admin
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25530490, AZND proxy owner() returned 0x8b5f269f...0068, accessManager() returned 0xe683fcd4...b520, that AccessManager returned true for DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on the same EOA, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot resolved to 0x2e49c14a...0db6. Verified source shows the OFT owner can change trusted peers, inbound trusted LayerZero messages mint through _credit, and UUPS _authorizeUpgrade requires the AccessManager default admin. The EOA therefore can authorize the Ethereum spoke mint path and replace mint-critical implementation logic.

review.evidence: Mu Digital documents KYC-gated primary minting through PrimaryMarket. At Monad block 87687688, verified AZND source and RPC reads resolve three TOKEN_MINTER_ROLE holders and the AccessManager default admin; the token is a direct non-proxy deployment with immutable PrimaryMarket but mutable role membership. At Ethereum block 25530490, verified OFT/UUPS source and RPC reads resolve the spoke proxy implementation, owner, AccessManager, and same 0x8b5f...0068 EOA as upgrade admin. Ethereum owner minting is indirect through trusted LayerZero peer configuration and UUPS control, not a public owner-only mint function.
